title: Beyond the 956: Florida cop arrested after allegedly taking over a dead man's home and identity for years
excerpt: Lauderhill officer Brian Louis Sguros, 35, faces five felonies after investigators say he took possession of Dennis West's home weeks after finding the 71-year-old dead on a welfare check in 2022 — paying taxes and utilities in West's name, forging his signature on a building permit, and using police databases to research him.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

LAUDERHILL, Fla. — A South Florida police officer who answered a welfare check and found a dead man inside his home is now charged with stealing that man's identity and taking over his house for years, according to investigators.

Brian Louis Sguros, 35, an officer with the Lauderhill Police Department, was one of the officers who responded to a welfare check at a home on N.W. 12th Street on July 11, 2022, after a neighbor called 911, concerned about a 71-year-old neighbor who had not been seen in more than a week. Inside, officers found the homeowner, Dennis Ionis West, dead. The medical examiner later determined West had died of natural causes, caused by cardiovascular disease.

Investigators with the Broward County Sheriff's Office say that shortly after West's death, Sguros told the Broward County Medical Examiner's Office that he had been West's friend and that West had no living family. Both claims were false, detectives said — there is no indication Sguros knew West before the welfare check.

According to a 21-page arrest affidavit, Sguros allegedly took possession of West's home on Aug. 1, 2022 — weeks after the body was found — without any legal authority, later admitting the takeover in a sworn court document. Over the following years, investigators say, Sguros paid the home's property taxes and utility bills in West's name, forged West's signature — and used a notary's name and seal — on a City of Lauderhill building-permit application, and repeatedly searched police computer databases for West's personal records without authorization.

Sguros claimed he spent more than $214,000 of his own money refurbishing the home, telling investigators he did it to protect the property from squatters and criminal activity. Investigators say the renovations raised the property's value to about $500,000. In February 2025, Sguros filed paperwork with the Broward County Property Appraiser's Office claiming his possession of the property dated back to August 2022. The scheme unraveled when West's rightful heirs sold the home and the buyer's representatives reportedly found Sguros living inside.

Sguros was placed on paid administrative leave on July 22 while the investigation ran, and was arrested on Tuesday, October 20, 2026. He now faces five felony offenses, including criminal use of a deceased person's personal identification information, criminal use of personal identification information, official misconduct, and an offense against computer users. After his arrest, he was placed on leave without pay.

The charges are allegations, and Sguros is presumed innocent unless and until he is convicted in court. The investigation remains active.

Sources: Broward County Sheriff's Office arrest affidavit, as reported by FOX 13 Tampa Bay, the New York Post, and the Palm Beach Post, Oct. 20–21, 2026; WorldStar (@worldstar) on Instagram, Oct. 21, 2026.
